Subject: Post-demo: grounding stress probes, retriever hyperparams, and reranker choice

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — great conversation and clear signal that Lumina's care navigation is a high-fit use case for a RAG-backed assistant. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the next steps and a lightweight set of asks to help us scope a short qualification eval.

1) What we observed / hypothesis
- Your support docs are moderately long with lots of semi-structured sections (protocols, product specs, and faq entries).
- Risk: hallucination surface when responses require exact coverage of protocols. We recommend prioritizing grounding recall + reranker precision over aggressive recall for the first pass.

2) Proposed quick eval (2-week):
- Deliverables: probe set (you provide positives/negatives + a handful of real tickets), initial retrieval config, reranker candidate list, and token-level benchmark PDF.
- Benchmarks: precision@1 on grounded facts, exact-match for critical protocol steps, and a short latency SLO for end-to-end responses.

3) Questions for your team (quick):
- Could you share ~50 sample tickets (anonymized) and 20 canonical protocol pages we should prioritize?
- Which models are you comfortable us using on a dev sandbox (open models OK) — any hard constraints on quantization/FP16?

4) Ops asks from Redwood side
- We'll generate a probe-set CSV and initial retrieval configs (Embeddings model + index chunk size + candidate pool size).
- Expect a short joint triage call to align metrics and anchor examples.

Attachments: demo recording, probe-set template (CSV), initial benchmark template (PDF).

Proposed next step: a 30-minute technical kickoff on Tue Mar 23 or Wed Mar 24 to lock the probe set and retrieval hyperparams. Are you available?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: grounding stress probes, retriever hyperparams, and reranker choice — ops recs

Thanks for the context. Quick recommendations we can present in the kickoff:

1) Retriever + index sizing
- Chunk size: 512 tokens per chunk for protocol pages (keeps passages focused, reduces false positives).
- Candidate pool: start with 100 candidates, evaluate P@1/P@5 — move to 250 only if recall is poor.
- Index type: vector index with doc metadata for section-level filtering (page id, section id).

2) Embeddings + encoder choices
- Embeddings: use a dense open embedding (e.g., small BGE or similar) for initial runs — cheaper for many vectors.
- Reranker: propose two lanes:
  a) Lightweight lane: bi-encoder reranker (sentence-transformer) — low-cost, good for P@3, near-instant latency.
  b) Precision lane: cross-encoder (distil-cross or moderate-sized cross-attention) for P@1 when grounding critical steps — higher compute and latency.

3) Prompting & model fit notes
- Models: recommend trying two LLM variants — an instruction-tuned open model (latency-friendly) and a higher-accuracy variant for the precision lane. We'll attach a short benchmark comparing them on a small subset.
- Prompting: include a strict grounding instruction with citation requirement and a fallback 'I don't know' token to reduce hallucination. We'll include prompt templates in the probe set.

4) Eval metrics to prioritize
- P@1 with citation accuracy, fact-exact-match for protocol steps, and a small hallucination rate diagnostic (we'll label hallucinations in the probe set).

I'll bring an ops config cheat-sheet to the call. Sean, if you can confirm latency targets we can put rough throughput numbers.

—Karthik

All — confirming latency/throughput guidance for the kickoff and subsequent sandbox runs:
- Baseline latency target (end-to-end, gen+retrieval+rerank): 450ms p50, 900ms p95 for initial sandbox; we'll tune after the first 100 probes.
- If we use cross-encoder reranker in production path, suggest async rerank with candidate thresholding to keep p95 under 1.5s.
- For the initial eval, we'll propose a light SLA: 1-2 qps sustained with bursts to 8 qps so your infra team can simulate realistic load.

I'll join the Wed 10am PT kickoff and bring a short runbook for how we instrument latency in the probe harness.

—Sean
